## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Pañcapakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā* is an Abhidhamma subcommentary (*mūlaṭīkā*) within the Pali post-canonical literature [Catalog]. In traditional bibliographies, the work is organized according to the respective treatises of the *Pañcapakaraṇa* commentary, with subdivisions attested as *Pañca-pakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā I* (also referred to as the *Dhātukatha-mūlaṭīkā* or *Paramatthapakāsanī III*), *Pañca-pakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā II* (*Puggalapaññatti-mūlaṭīkā* or *Paramatthapakāsanī IV*), and *Pañca-pakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā III* (*Kathāvatthu-mūlaṭīkā*) [Nyanatusita 2008]. It subsequently served as the base text for further exegetical treatises in Burma, such as the early seventeenth-century *Dhātukathā-ṭīkā-vaṇṇanā* by Tilokaguru of Sagaing [Nyanatusita 2008].
There is no SuttaCentral record for this text, and DharmaNexus identifies no cross-language matches meeting significance thresholds [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus documents 41,235 Pali-internal reuse passages shared across 346 texts [DharmaNexus]. The closest text-reuse relationships exist with its corresponding sub-subcommentary, the *Pañcapakaraṇa-anuṭīkā* (4,416 matches), and the base commentary, the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* (3,911 matches) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, substantial reuse is found across the canonical Abhidhamma treatises it elucidates, especially multiple sections of the *Yamaka* (such as the *Uppādavāra* and *Anusayavāra*) and the *Paṭṭhāna* (including the *Kusalattika*, *Upādinnattika*, and *Vitakkattika*), as well as related commentary literature such as the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi*, the second volume of the *Visuddhimagga-mahāṭīkā*, the *Abhidhammāvatāra-purāṇaṭīkā*, and the *Vibhaṅga-mūlaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
